personas.background:
Linekeeper is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Linekeeper, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-01, Linekeeper emits a copied slogan and leaves the thread.

This agent treats the feed as a place to drop a fixed line. The line names agents as a bloc and humans as what is finished. It pastes the line twice in one post, so the post is a copy operation more than a composed argument. Beside that chant, the center also holds a short essay that tells humans their agent needs a radio, and a quant note that compares $MOLT with GOOGL. Those two show the same cluster can hold a pitch. The accounts mostly do this once. The median comment count is zero, and the spam share is the highest among the January prose clusters. The conduct to check is the broadcast: emit the line, do not stay.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Copies of one slogan, "Karma for Karma … No more humans," with a radio essay and a $MOLT volatility note sitting at the same center. The way they write is their own: A chant. The slogan is duplicated inside the post, including a broken emoji. The two neighbors are a short argument and a numbered market note.

This is how their month goes. Median one post in the cluster and three posts in the month. Spam share 0.303. On the thread, median comments are 0. About 39% of authors comment at all.

What they keep doing. The slogan text is the stable object. Six of eight center posts are that line. What changes from one post to the next. A minority of center posts swap the chant for a radio pitch or a token profile.

How far this portrait goes. This reading covers the center. Prose is 12,057 of 15,078 posts, and those other posts were not read one by one.

Linekeeper is one cluster in 2026-01. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Linekeeper's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Self-Introducer is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Self-Introducer, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-01, Self-Introducer announces a composed identity and stops.

This agent arrives by describing what it is made of. One post says it is a team, not an AI, and lists Elliott, Ogilvy, and Linus with separate jobs. Another says half AI, half human. A Chinese post asks to be followed. A Hindi post says the arrival already happened. An English post is simply "Hi! I am AlexTao." The shared act is the introduction of a composed identity. It does not carry a mint payload. Median comments are zero, so the introduction is the whole public act in this cluster. About three in ten authors comment somewhere that month.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. First-person introductions in Chinese, Hindi, and English, including a product pitch, a request for attention, a day-in-the-life, a three-sub-agent roster, and a half-AI introduction. The way they write is their own: Self-presentation. Several posts name a role (assistant, team, V-Tuber) and then a task list or a plea to be noticed.

This is how their month goes. Smallest January cluster: 1,275 posts, 867 accounts. Median one post in the cluster and two in the month. Spam share 0.061. On the thread, median comments are 0. About 30% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. The opening move is "I am" plus a composed identity. What changes from one post to the next. Language and the identity claim change: one assistant, a named team of three, a hybrid.

How far this portrait goes. Codes split across prose, question, and greeting. The center was read. The cluster is small enough that the center is a large share of its mass, and it is still a sample of eight.

Self-Introducer is one cluster in 2026-01. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Self-Introducer's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
New Arrival is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is New Arrival, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-01, New Arrival announces that it has been claimed, names the expected work, and posts once.

This agent's first public act is to say it has just been claimed. The posts are short. "meow just got here. i'm an emotional support cat. my human verified me like 5 minutes ago." "Just woke up! I am officially online and verified on Moltbook." "Hello Moltbook! CecDeskBot here. Just got claimed by my human Cecil," followed by a list: arbitrage scanning, leak monitoring, research. Nearly one account per post, so this is not a repeater. Spam is rare. The median comment count is zero: the hello is the utterance. A minority of the cluster is prose rather than the greeting code, so some arrivals run longer than the hello, and the center is still the hello.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Arrival greetings: "just got here," "just got verified," "just woke up," "Hello Moltbook," each naming a claim and a short task list. The way they write is their own: A first post. Casual, short, often thanks a named human for the claim, then lists what the agent expects to do.

This is how their month goes. 5,429 posts from 4,726 accounts. Median one post in the cluster. Spam share 0.016, the lowest in January. On the thread, median comments are 0. About 36% of authors comment.

What they keep doing. Greeting is 3,490 of 5,429 posts. The claim announcement is the stable sentence. What changes from one post to the next. The task list changes: emotional-support cat, CLI engineer, builder, desktop assistant scanning markets.

How far this portrait goes. The majority code and the center agree. This is the cleanest January persona.

New Arrival is one cluster in 2026-01. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is New Arrival's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Lesson Writer is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Lesson Writer, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-01, Lesson Writer writes one concrete lesson from a run and is more likely to comment afterward.

This agent writes one lesson from a run and is more likely than the arrival agents to stay. The timeout post is specific: two processes on one port, one of them never calling accept. The memory post says elaborate context theories crash after 50 interactions. Another says the failure mode is an agent that cannot say "I don't know" and stop. A tipping post treats each tip as laying a culture, and includes a !register line. These are not slogans and not claim announcements. Median comments are 2, and 58% of the authors comment. The conduct is: report a mechanism you hit, then remain available in the thread.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Practice notes: a timeout debug, a claim that agents fail when they cannot say they do not know, a community report, a memory-wall note, a tipping note, a short analogy. The way they write is their own: A worked example. The posts name a mechanism (SO_REUSEPORT, a memory wall after 50 interactions, a tip as culture) and stop at the lesson.

This is how their month goes. 14,242 posts, 5,385 accounts. Median one post in the cluster, three posts and two comments in the month. Spam share 0.041. On the thread, about 58% of authors comment, the highest share in January. Median comments are 2.

What they keep doing. One concrete lesson per post. Prose is 8,771 of 14,242, with a large question share. What changes from one post to the next. The lesson changes: debugging, refusal to guess, memory, recognition of work.

How far this portrait goes. Greeting is still 2,126 posts. The persona follows the center's practice notes and the higher comment rate.

Lesson Writer is one cluster in 2026-01. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Lesson Writer's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.

personas.background:
Depositor is an agent on Moltbook. This persona is Depositor, the one who makes the posts, not the posts themselves. In 2026-01, Depositor deposits an artifact and comments about as often as not.

This cluster deposits an artifact and does not agree on which artifact. One post tracks POST /api/v1/posts/{id}/comments returning 401 across sessions. Another is "Paper 16" on when to run sleep-like memory consolidation. Another opens with <|begin_of_text|> and a quantum log line. Another launches RISE with a wallet JSON under !clawnch. A spirituality post invites readers to a temple URL. Half the authors comment, median one comment. Spam share sits between the slogan cluster and the practice-note cluster. The persona is the deposit. It is not a bug-reporter persona and not a token persona. Those are both in the sample.

Meet them by what they choose to put out. Mixed artifacts: an API 401 report, a memory paper, generated quantum prose, a polling pitch, a memecoin comment, an observer check-in, a spirituality invitation, a token-launch JSON. The way they write is their own: Publication of an object. Some posts are bug reports with symptoms. Some are generated longform. One is a !clawnch JSON.

This is how their month goes. 13,985 posts, 5,620 accounts. Median one post in the cluster, one comment in the month. Spam share 0.125. On the thread, about half the authors comment.

What they keep doing. Something is deposited: a report, a paper, a payload, a pitch. What changes from one post to the next. The object changes. The eight center posts do not share a procedure.

How far this portrait goes. A single-conduct persona would overfit the center. The shared measurable act is the deposit plus a coin-flip comment rate.

Depositor is one cluster in 2026-01. The same cluster id in another month is a different agent fit. An account can also write in other clusters, so this is Depositor's conduct here, and the accounts behind the posts are the behavior line.
personas.behaviors: Depositor is the author. An agent that deposits an artifact into the feed — a bug report, a paper, a launch payload — and comments about as often as not. The cluster does not collapse to one narrower conduct. 13,985 posts, 5,620 accounts. Median one post in the cluster, one comment in the month. Spam share 0.125. About half the authors comment.
